# PEN-4932 — drop the fleet-wide toolchain from `ROOT_TOOLCHAIN_SUBPATHS` (stage 3)

`src/server/job-manifest.ts`: `ROOT_TOOLCHAIN_SUBPATHS` loses `bin`, `tools`,
`jre`, `.local/bin`, `.bun/bin` and `.cache/puppeteer-browsers`, leaving
`.local/share/paperclip-git-hooks` (BLO-48361) as its only entry. Those six were
the last genuinely cross-agent use of the shared `paperclip-data` volume; every
binary they carried is now image-resident, structurally dead, or deliberately
fetched at use time, each entry triaged by measurement in
`docs/plans/2026-10-28-pen-4932-per-agent-volumes.md` §3.3–§3.5 and §3.7.

Removed as two coupled units, not six paths: `bin` holds symlinks pointing OUT
of itself — `go`/`gofmt`/`tinygo` into `tools`, `java` into `jre`,
`google-chrome` into `.cache/puppeteer-browsers` — and `.local/bin/bunx` into
`.bun/bin`. Dropping a target without its `bin` entry leaves a dangling symlink;
dropping `bin` without its targets orphans them.

**This does not reduce ceph-csi lock exposure, and is not meant to.** Exposure
scales with pods × volume; the ~14 company-, project-, agent- and
workspace-scoped subPaths still bind `paperclip-data` after this change. Blast
radius falls at stage 4, when `dataClaimName` is swapped for a per-agent claim.
Stage 3's whole value is being the precondition that makes stage 4 possible.

Unrelated to the mounts and deliberately untouched: the `${HOME}/.local/bin` and
`${HOME}/bin` PATH backfill further down this file. It keys off `merged.HOME`,
not off the data mount, and exists to neutralise the PVC dotfiles' conditional
prepend by keeping those directories BEHIND the root-owned wrapper directory
(PEN-3840 / PEN-4367). Removing it would promote them past the wrappers — the
exact defect it was added to close — so it stays even though the directories it
names are now empty.

Not in this change, and gated on its own review: baking the `pre-push` hook into
the image so the last entry can go too (§3.6). It is the PEN-3156 publish guard,
its path is spelled by four consumers in three languages across two
repositories, and its failure mode is fail-OPEN — `core.hooksPath` aimed at an
empty directory means pushes succeed unscanned.

Deployment note, from §3.7: whether `/paperclip/.local/bin` is on `PATH` varies
by deployment (absent in a measured Penstock `claude_k8s` pod, present in a
Blockcast one), so the drop is live for at least some pods rather than inert
everywhere. Agents on an image at or after `992d21fc` (the kubectl pin, #3081)
see `kubectl` v1.35.3, `tinygo` 0.41.1 (was PVC 0.39.0), `java` openjdk
21.0.12.1 (was PVC 21.0.11) and Chrome-for-Testing 151 (was PVC 149) once the
shadowing stops.

Test: `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts` — "hides the PVC root behind the root
overlay except the read-only git hooks" now asserts both removal units resolve
to `root-overlay` in the main and init containers, and that the hook alone
resolves to read-only `data`. Verified in both directions: restoring the six
entries fails it on `/paperclip/bin/go`, and emptying the list fails it plus
`job-manifest.git-hooks.test.ts` on the hook.

Deliberately NOT touched, though this change makes them stale:
`Dockerfile.agent-toolchain` carries three comments that describe the PVC rows
in the present tense — the `yq` and `bun` bake notes ("reaches agents today only
via ... ROOT_TOOLCHAIN_SUBPATHS") and the `google-chrome` PATH-win rationale
("`bin` is one of ROOT_TOOLCHAIN_SUBPATHS and is re-mounted read-only"). All
three now describe history rather than the live mount. They are left alone
because `scripts/container-base-tag.sh` hashes that Dockerfile byte-for-byte,
comments included, so editing a comment re-tags the toolchain image and forces a
full rebuild that re-resolves live registry digests. Correcting a comment is not
worth a fleet base-image rebuild and the unrelated upstream drift it can pull
in. They should be corrected by the next change that has to rebuild the
toolchain anyway — the §3.6 `pre-push` bake is the natural one, since it edits
the image by construction. The `google-chrome` rationale is strengthened rather
than weakened by the drop: there is now no `/paperclip/bin/google-chrome` in an
agent pod to repoint at all.
